flagged.location: ## Statement, conclusions using C and N_C(x_*)
flagged.evidence: The Statement says “Let the equalities be Ax=b” and concludes “global minimizer over the feasible set C” and “-∇f(x*)∈N_C(x*)”, but does not define C or specify the finite inequality index range. Its generic-program dependency defines C as {x∈U:h(x)=0, g_i(x)≤0 (1≤i≤m)}; this Statement never identifies h(x)=Ax-b. The two uses of C therefore have no bound subject.

Step 1.2 asserts that “the map R_J(y)=G_J^{-1}A_J^Ty is continuous” and then uses its closed preimage, while [F1] supplies only closedness of finite-dimensional subspaces. The proof gives no continuity estimate for this matrix map. The bound ||R_J(y)-R_J(y')||₂≤||G_J^{-1}A_J^T||₂||y-y'||₂ closes this short gap.

[F1] says feasibility gives a unique minimizer “with a KKT certificate” on an independent support. Step 1.2 applies that existence result to an arbitrary accepted candidate and says [F1] identifies the candidate with the minimizer. Existence of one KKT certificate does not establish that every feasible KKT candidate is optimal; the proof needs universal KKT sufficiency or a direct convexity argument.

flagged.location: Facts & Assumptions [F3], applied in Proof step 4.1
flagged.evidence: [F3] attributes the claim that “any feasible KKT tuple is a global certificate” to lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproblem-has-unique-kkt-certificate. That lemma’s Statement asserts existence of multipliers at its unique minimizer and says “This KKT tuple certifies the global minimizer”; it does not state sufficiency for every feasible KKT tuple. Step 4.1 uses the stronger universal claim for the algorithm’s terminal tuple.

Step 3.1 relies on [F4] to conclude global optimality. The current Statement of thm-convex-kkt-sufficiency-and-normal-cone-certificate leaves C undefined and does not bind it to this example’s displayed feasible set. The example’s conclusion is correct, but this citation does not formally license it as written; a direct lower bound from x₁+x₂≥1 and ||x||₂²≥(x₁+x₂)²/2 closes the gap.
